description: ALL IN ONE Hacking Tool For Hackers

Categories include password recovery alongside phishing, payload creation, post-exploitation, DDoS and wireless tools.
README describes list-form subprocesses, verified downloads, an SBOM and per-step confirmation; implementation was not audited here.
The tool is a broad launcher, while JEFFE's implemented product scope is local offline recovery.
reason: Retain discoverability and architecture references. Use direct reviewed recovery-engine adapters rather than importing a broad attack launcher or its installers.

description: All-in-One Hacking Tools For Hackers! And more hacking tools! For termux.

description: Modular personalized dictionary generator.
observations: README describes nine small Unix-style C/shell dictionary-transformation tools communicating through text streams.
The project's wizard requests target information; that profiling flow is outside the chosen recovery-product scope.
Generic transformations could apply to an explicitly user-supplied recovery vocabulary, but John already offers overlapping rules.
The README claims a four-keyword example expands to more than two million entries, highlighting the need for output limits.
GitHub metadata reports GPL-3.0; README wording also references GPLv3+, requiring exact file-level review before reuse.
reason: Potential optional local subprocess integration for user-supplied vocabularies only. Benchmark value versus existing John rules, review source/license, and enforce bounded output before enabling; no integration was executed.

description: This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass the credentials brute-force prevention mechanism of the Embedded Web Server (interface) of more than 60 Lexmark printer models. This issue affects both username-password and PIN authentication.

README links the Lexmark security advisory and describes testing on three printer models.
This is a live authentication-control bypass PoC, not an offline recovery engine.
reason: Keep the CVE and advisory as defensive reference metadata. Do not implement login brute-force or bypass orchestration in an offline recovery workbench.

description: Integrate 183 pentesting and OSINT tools into Claude Code to execute security tasks via local backends or Docker containers.
observations: README claims a Claude Code wrapper around 183 tools using native Bash, WSL or Docker.
Many unrelated project and screenshot links point to the same ZIP under this repository instead of their claimed destinations.
README installation instructions name AKCODEZ/hackingtool-plugin while the supplied repository is MAXZL1/hackingtool-plugin.
README advertises retrying commands with elevated privileges after permission failures.
GitHub metadata returns no license, and the inspected root has no LICENSE file.
No ZIP, executable, plugin skill or installation script was downloaded or run; these observations do not establish malware.
reason: Retain only reference metadata pending origin, license and payload verification. Link inconsistencies and advertised automatic privilege escalation make automatic installation inappropriate.

description: This project offers a straightforward solution for retrieving forgotten PDF passwords using Google Colab. With just five simple steps, it efficiently handles passwords of any complexity. Say goodbye to PDF access hurdles and hello to seamless password recovery.
observations: The repository contains a Colab notebook, README and GPL license, rather than a reusable packaged recovery service.
Notebook attempts actual PDF password verification with pikepdf.open; this is candidate-based recovery, not merely removal of PDF permission flags or decryption using an already-known password.
The generator stores every candidate in an in-memory list and writes passwordlist.txt; the verifier prints attempted and recovered plaintext passwords.
README requires uploading the PDF to Google Colab and makes broad compatibility claims that were not independently validated.
reason: Use as a workflow reference only. Prefer a local, independently reviewed PDF library or John's existing PDF converter; do not execute the Colab notebook or inherit its unbounded candidate memory, secret printing, or universal-recovery claims.
validation: Read-only metadata, README, tree, and selected source inspection; not installed, executed, or benchmarked.

description: PDF Crack is a GUI tool used for cracking pdf passwords. includes 3 cracking options
license: No root license; lth-pdfcrack/README.md states 'Internal LTH tool. All rights reserved.'

The README's speedup figures (up to 47x/100x) are upstream claims, not benchmark results from this review.
The nested README explicitly reserves rights and no top-level LICENSE was found in the inspected tree.
reason: Do not copy or redistribute its source without permission. Record the feature reference, but rely on licensed existing engines for local PDF recovery.
